subChunks.title: Extending Classes

storyBeats.text: Eldrin unrolls the Academy's great lineage scroll. At the top: Wizard. Below it, branching like a tree: FireWizard, IceWizard, StormWizard, each inheriting the foundation.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Inheritance models an IS-A relationship. A FireWizard is a Wizard. It inherits everything — name, level, the ability to greet — and adds its own specialisation on top.

storyBeats.label: FireWizard in action

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Notice super(n) — the first thing any child constructor does is call its parent's constructor. The parent must be fully built before the child can add its own enchantments.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Create a class Animal with a protected String name and a method speak() that prints "...". Create Dog extends Animal with its own speak() that prints "[name] says: Woof!". Create Cat extends Animal printing "[name] says: Meow!". Construct one of each and call speak().
guidedPractice.hint: Use super(name) in Dog and Cat constructors. Override speak() in each subclass.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain inheritance in Java. What is the IS-A relationship, and what does the super() call do in a child constructor?

questions.prompt: Which keyword is used in Java to inherit from a parent class?
questions.explanation: extends establishes an inheritance relationship. implements is used for interfaces, not class inheritance.

questions.prompt: A child class in Java can extend multiple parent classes simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Java supports only single inheritance for classes. A class can extend only one parent. Multiple interface implementation is allowed instead.

subChunks.title: Overriding, Abstract & final

storyBeats.text: Eldrin draws the Shape archetype on the board — no specific form, just a promise that every shape will know its own area.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: An abstract class is an incomplete blueprint — a template that mandates certain behaviours without specifying how. You cannot conjure a raw Shape, but you can conjure a Circle or Rectangle that fulfils the Shape contract.

storyBeats.label: Shape hierarchy

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: And final — the seal of completion. A final class may not be extended; its design is closed. Use it when you must guarantee a class's behaviour can never be altered by subclasses.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Create abstract class Shape with abstract method area(). Implement Rectangle (width × height) and Triangle (0.5 × base × height). Create one of each and call area().
guidedPractice.hint: Rectangle needs width and height fields; Triangle needs base and height. Both should override area().

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is an abstract class in Java? How does it differ from a concrete class and from an interface?

options: Asks the compiler to verify you are correctly overriding a parent method
Forces the method to replace all parent code
questions.answer: Asks the compiler to verify you are correctly overriding a parent method
questions.explanation: @Override is optional but recommended — it tells the compiler to check that a matching method exists in the parent. If not, it gives a compile error, preventing silent bugs from typos.
super.hello() calls the parent version first (prints "A"), then the child version continues (prints "B").

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about abstract classes is correct?
options: An abstract class can have both abstract and concrete methods
An abstract class must have only abstract methods
You can create instances of an abstract class directly
An abstract class cannot have constructors
questions.answer: An abstract class can have both abstract and concrete methods
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can mix abstract methods (no body, must be overridden) with concrete methods (have a body, can be inherited or overridden). They cannot be instantiated directly but can have constructors for subclasses to call via super().
